clue.text: Wishful thinking grips novelist right? Cherry-pie

indicators.note: the first piece holds the next pieces inside it, as a hand grips something

parts.note: hope is wishful thinking
George Eliot was the novelist who wrote Middlemarch

explanation.surface: A hopeful question about whether some novelist has got things right, ending oddly with a pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grips' signals the container. Cherry-pie is an old garden name for this purple, sweet-scented flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherry-pie is a cottage-garden name for the plant, whose flowers smell of baked fruit.

clue.text: Drug used by Jack Ketch

explanation.surface: A notorious figure from history caught out using narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Ketch was a seventeenth-century English executioner, whose rope was made of this fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannabis is a narcotic from the plant, and the same plant's fibre made the hangman's rope.

clue.text: Awkward rascals, these eastern sailors

indicators.note: awkward suggests something put together clumsily, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint about troublesome rogues who happen to be seamen from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Lascars were seamen from India and South-East Asia serving on European ships.

clue.text: Music-maker or bird (including what was left of the Cheshire Cat)

indicators.note: including means the bird's name takes the cat's remnant within it

parts.note: a gander is a male goose

parts.words: what was left of the Cheshire Cat
parts.note: in Alice in Wonderland the Cheshire Cat fades away until only its grin remains

explanation.surface: A riddle offering a musician or a bird, with a nod to Lewis Carroll's vanishing cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' signals the container; 'or' is taken as it is, not as a link between two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A street musician turning the handle of a barrel organ makes music.

clue.text: Learner Bruce in new form of hat worn by Mr. Lear

indicators.note: a new form means these letters are reshaped into a different word

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate letter

explanation.surface: A learner named Bruce trying on a remodelled version of Edward Lear's headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new form of' rearranges L, BRUCE and IN. In Lear's nonsense verse the Dong and others wear a hat described with this made-up word.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear's nonsense verse speaks of a runcible hat, so the coined adjective describes his headgear.

clue.text: This type of order is after all incomplete

parts.note: post is a Latin prefix meaning after

indicators.note: incomplete means the word all loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain sort of instruction is, after all, unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' drops the last L of ALL, leaving AL. A postal order is a British money certificate bought at a post office.
explanation.definitionFit: A postal order is a money voucher sent through the mail, so the word names that kind of order.

clue.text: Soft butter in a vessel

parts.note: P stands for piano, soft in music
a ram is an animal that butts

explanation.surface: A soft spread of butter served in a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the spread but something that butts. The definition is a flat-bottomed boat, not the baby carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A pram is also a small flat-bottomed boat, a kind of craft.

clue.text: Provide substitutes for corded and fancy fabrics

parts.note: rep is a fabric with a corded, ribbed surface
lace is an ornamental openwork fabric

explanation.surface: A draper swapping in ribbed and decorative materials.
explanation.definitionFit: To substitute something is to put a new item in the old one's place.

clue.text: Trading vessel lit up in the lake

indicators.note: in places the vessel and turned word within the lake

parts.note: a mere is a lake
a can is a container

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

explanation.surface: A merchant ship lit up out on the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses; 'in' signals the container, with 'the' part of the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercantile means concerned with commerce and merchants.

clue.text: Shunning the fair sex he is into gyms for a change

indicators.note: a change signals that these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man avoiding women decides to take up going to the gym instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges IS INTO GYMS. The definition includes 'he': the man who shuns women.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman-hater avoids female company, the fair sex being an old phrase for women.

clue.text: Box, knocks being returned

indicators.note: being returned means the word for knocks is sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: raps are knocks

explanation.surface: A boxer's blows coming back at him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being returned' turns RAPS backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box for practice.

clue.text: Scene of topping achievement to herald the coronation

definitions.text: Scene of topping achievement to herald the coronation

parts.words: Scene of topping achievement to herald the coronation
parts.note: the world's highest summit was first climbed in 1953, news arriving on the day Elizabeth II was crowned

explanation.surface: Where the greatest feat took place, just in time for the crowning.
explanation.walkthrough: Hillary and Tenzing's ascent in 1953 was announced in London on the morning of the coronation; 'topping' is literal, reaching the top.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan peak was the scene of the first ascent, reported on coronation day.

clue.text: Principal event in cockfighting

explanation.surface: The headline bout at a cockfight.
explanation.walkthrough: In cockfighting a main was a match of several fights between birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Chief or chief one in the first sense; a set match between gamecocks in the second.

clue.text: Beloved by 12 perhaps, or a word of thanks

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of the other answer may be ordered differently

parts.note: the answer to 12 across is main
ta is a British informal thank you

explanation.surface: A sweetheart won by someone, or simply a thank-you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges MAIN (the answer to 12) into INAM; then OR A as written and TA.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a female lover or sweetheart.

clue.text: Stipple a manuscript to form no original writing

indicators.note: to form means the letters are shaped into a new word

explanation.surface: Dotting a manuscript to create something with no first draft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to form' rearranges STIPPLE, A and MS.
explanation.definitionFit: A palimpsest is a parchment scraped clean and reused, so its first text is gone.

clue.text: Competently consumed an irrational quantity in a ridiculous fashion

indicators.note: consumed means the first word swallows the second

parts.note: ably means competently
a surd is an irrational number such as the square root of two

explanation.surface: Someone efficiently eating an absurd amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed' signals the container. In maths a surd is a root that cannot be written as a fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Done preposterously, beyond reason.

clue.text: Resolved like Achilles to sulk here?

explanation.surface: A determined Greek hero retreats to brood.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Iliad Achilles sulked in his tent, so the second reading splits as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Determined, set on a purpose; and, split, inside a canvas shelter where Achilles brooded.

clue.text: Murphy will naturally lead a dull life

explanation.surface: Murphy is bound to end up living a boring existence.
explanation.walkthrough: Murphy is slang for a potato, which as a vegetable naturally does this.
explanation.definitionFit: A potato grows like a plant; to live idly and monotonously is the second sense.

clue.text: One's country, if for instance a Cypriot

definitions.text: One's country, if for instance a Cypriot

parts.note: one is I, so one's is I'S
land means a country

explanation.surface: A Cypriot describing his homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'One's country' as I'S LAND; Cyprus is an island, so a Cypriot's country is one.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyprus is surrounded by sea, so a Cypriot's homeland is a piece of land in water.

clue.text: He made a bit of gold in a ship

indicators.note: in places the heraldic metal within the ship

parts.note: a liner is a passenger ship
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A man who made some gold aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container. A bit here is the mouthpiece of a horse's bridle, not a small piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A loriner made metal bridle fittings such as bits and spurs.

clue.text: Change of fortune making no difference to Laval

explanation.surface: A political comeback that changes nothing for Laval.
explanation.walkthrough: Laval reads the same backwards, so turning it round leaves it unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn of luck for the worse; and a backwards reading, which leaves a palindrome as it was.

clue.text: Support needed by those on board

definitions.text: Support needed by those on board

parts.words: Support needed by those on board
parts.note: the support is the steadiness of a sailor's balance on a rolling deck, not a structure

explanation.surface: Something holding up passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors need the ability to keep their balance on a moving ship.

clue.text: Advertised as pipes may be

explanation.surface: Tobacco pipes promoted in an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: Promoted with exaggerated praise; and drawn on in short breaths, as a smoker's pipe is.

clue.text: Harry is essentially attractive

parts.note: per se is Latin for in itself, essentially
cute means attractive

explanation.surface: A description of a man called Harry as fundamentally good-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' is the verb, to harass, not a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to harass or hound someone.

clue.text: Dash across the Channel

parts.note: dash means verve, and the word for it is French, from over the water from Britain

explanation.surface: A quick crossing of the English Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair and spirit, a loan word from French.

clue.text: USA's standard state representative

parts.note: the standard is the flag, on which each state is represented by one emblem

explanation.surface: An ordinary congressman for an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the fifty points on the Stars and Stripes stands for a state.

clue.text: Bird makes writer Laurence lose his way

indicators.note: lose means the writer's name drops the letters for the road

parts.note: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A bird causes a novelist to get lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose' takes ST from the front of STERNE.
explanation.definitionFit: An erne is a sea eagle.

clue.text: Obliteration of six notes intended to be heard

parts.note: E, F, F, A, C, E are six musical notes

indicators.note: to be heard signals the word for intended is spoken, sounding like other letters

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A musical passage of six notes, purposefully played aloud, that wipes everything out.
explanation.walkthrough: The six notes are the note names E F F A C E; 'to be heard' makes MEANT sound like MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiping out or erasing something completely.

clue.text: Spare one for the driver-exhaust, say?

indicators.note: say means the word is spoken, standing for a word of the same sound

parts.note: to tire is to exhaust

explanation.surface: A motorist's spare part, perhaps the exhaust pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhaust' is not the car part but the verb to wear out. The spare carried in the boot is the wheel's rubber.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare wheel's rubber covering is carried by a motorist.

clue.text: Counsellor round central Perth who contributes to newspapers

indicators.note: round means the counsellor wraps around the next letters

parts.note: an adviser is a counsellor

indicators.note: central takes the middle letters of the city name, dropping its ends

explanation.surface: A counsellor travelling around the middle of an Australian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central' keeps all but the first and last letters of Perth, an Australian city; 'round' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pays for space in the press contributes to its pages.
